title: PM2.5 Episode Frequency by Wind Direction
dataSources: Seismograph events (`seismograph:event`), seismic noise (`seismograph:noise`), air quality (`airquality:reading`), radiation counts (`radiation:count`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), phenology observations (`phenology:observation`), and weather-station rainfall (`weatherstation:reading`).
app: Citizen-science telemetry from seismographs, weather stations, air-quality monitors, Geiger counters, lightning feeds, and phenology journals streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT, APIs, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=airquality:reading
| where pm25_ugm3>=35
| eval wind_sector=case(wind_deg<45 OR wind_deg>=315,"N",wind_deg<135,"E",wind_deg<225,"S",true(),"W")
| stats count as episodes by wind_sector
| sort - episodes
description: Counts unhealthy particulate episodes by wind sector to show which directions bring the dirtiest air to your site.
value: Air-quality spikes are more actionable when you know the direction they come from, whether that means traffic, wildfire, or a nearby burner.
implementation: Stream PM2.5 and wind direction from your particulate monitor or weather station and bucket them by sector.
visualization: Bar chart of high-PM2.5 episodes by wind sector.
grandmaExplanation: It logs which wind direction usually brings the dirtiest air to your home or yard.
